land_types.land_types_note: Land-type pass (tile_land_types.gd): shore marsh round painted water (12 cells round lakes under low_lake_m), treeline at about half the island summit (1245 m on island 8), evergreen belt on slopes over 0.2 tangent between belt_min_m and the treeline.

precarve.summit_crowns_note: [x, z, k, full_m, fade_m]: island 8 summit (1245 m) was a 120 m wide crown within 5 m of the top; this takes k x r^2 off the shoulders out to full_m so it reads under 100 m (island check).

note: Rules for turning the 160 m world elevation map into one tile's 8 m height map: smooth cubic upsampling plus fine detail noise that is continuous across tile borders. Rerun tools/build_tile.gd after editing.

frame.note: Each tile is built on a frame that reaches this many 8 m samples beyond its edge on every side, then cropped. Edge samples then see the same neighbors as the next tile's. Must be a multiple of the climate coarse step (4) and at least as far as the longest distance the climate looks at (600 m = 75 samples).

summit.note: A real peak on every summit of the world map (WorldElevation.summits): adds spire_share of the summit height as a tent that reaches radius_factor x that far, sharp for power above 1; capped at max_m. See GENERATOR_NOTES.md. 8 Nov 2026 (peaks that can stand, docs/water/watershed_rebuild_design.md A1): radius_factor 3.2 to 4.0 and power 1.7 to 1.3, so the tip slope (power / radius_factor) is 0.33 instead of 0.53; with the sketch's standing cones (sketch_rules standing.slope 0.32) the summit stays under 35 degrees, which any rock holds. spur_reach: along the summit's spurs (sketch_rules standing.tip_spurs) the tent reaches that much farther (gentler), so the spurs run on as ridges and the point is not round. spur_apex_share: the spurs fade in from the point to 2 x this share of the reach (WorldElevation.spur_weight_at), so the top is not drawn as a star of thin rays (run 8a38328c zooms).

rolling.note: Swells and knolls for low dry land (tile_rolling.gd), added after the water is carved and faded out near any water, so rivers and ponds keep their shape. octaves: wavelength and amplitude in meters. Strength rises from low_from_m to low_to_m of height (beaches stay calm), fades out between fade_from_m and fade_to_m (high ground uses the normal detail), and is zero within near_water_m of water and full beyond far_water_m. Times the island texture factor. See GENERATOR_NOTES.md.

hills.note: Dave 4 Nov 2026 (BUG-031, 'valleys and hills and rolling hills along the plains; way too flat, no character'): broad hills on the same low dry land, each octave 0 to amplitude_m high (power shapes them: above 1 rounder tops, wider vales), so the ground only rises away from the water and the rivers keep the low line of their valleys. Faded to nothing within near_water_m of water, full beyond far_water_m; their own height fade (fade_from_m to fade_to_m) lets them run up into the foothills (Dave 4 Nov: 'just need variety'); times the island texture but at least texture_min; level round the spawn pad. Closed hollows the hills make are filled to their spill (drain), so no new ponds.

octaves.note: Dave 5 Nov 2026: 'it should create some steeper but smaller hills', half the big hills' height on about a quarter of their width; power 2.5 keeps most ground low so these stand alone

detail.note: Noise octaves added on land. amplitude_m is the full strength; it fades in with height so beaches and the coastal plain stay smooth and the sea floor stays calm.

valleys.note: Owner (2026-10-19): rivers run at the bottom of real valleys. Around each world river the land is lowered toward the river's water level: a flat floor (floor_half_m each side, more for big rivers), then walls rising smoothly into the hills out to half_width_m (capped by half_width_max_m, which must stay under the frame margin of 640 m). Ground a little below the water beside the river is lifted up to lift_max_m. Detail noise on the floor is cut to detail_on_floor of its strength.

strata.note: Owner (2026-10-20): hard rock beds stand as ledges and cliffs with flat benches on top, soft beds wear into gentle slopes (tile_height.gd _add_strata). Heights in a hard bed are remapped: talus_part of the bed steepened by talus_steepen, then cliff_part made into the cliff, the rest flattened to bench_flatten. dip bends the beds over kilometers; country picks ledge country (above country_from, full at country_full) versus rounded hills.
strata.rock_note: With real rock (the baker) the beds are the geology layers and dip/country are not used; ledge strength comes from rock.ledges.

erosion.note: Erosion on a 32 m copy of the tile: water cuts valleys in proportion to how much flows through (stream power), slopes soften (diffusion). The change is added back onto the 8 m map. It fades out near the tile edges so neighboring tiles still match.
erosion.rock_note: Owner (2026-10-20): erosion knows the rock. Each point wears at the plain rate times soft_rate for the softest rock down to hard_rate for the hardest (geometric between, by rock.hardness), worked out from the rock at its current height every rock_refresh_iterations steps. River carving (water) ignores the rock.
erosion.mountain_note: Tyler (2026-10-21, M1): a second, stronger run (stream_k, iterations) blended in on high ground (from_m to full_m) (Dave 2026-10-21: height rule only, no place-specific masks): carves ridges and gullies in the mountains without moving lowlands, rivers, ponds or bays.

scree.note: Tyler (FINDINGS 9 B and 16 D, 2026-10-21): at the foot of every face steeper than cliff_deg the loose rock lies in a concave apron, top_deg against the face easing to toe_deg, height_share of the face height (at most max_height_m), length from the angles (min_length_m to max_length_m). It comes as fan tongues (tongue_min is the thinnest share between them, tongue_m the spacing along the face). Fill only (tile_scree.gd), after the ledges and before the rivers.

ore_cap.note: Owner (2026-10-20): ore under soil stays hidden. Where loose cover lies over rock, ore stops at least min_m (and the whole cover) below the surface; bare rock keeps its ore showing. In node_share of node_cell_m squares the ore is left exposed as a node (its top voxels turn to the host rock). terrain_generator.gd _fill_ore_column.

rock.note: Owner (2026-10-20): the land is made from its rock. hardness 0 (wears away fast) to 1 (stands): used by erosion. ledges 0 (none) to 1 (strong): how strongly an outcropping bed of that rock stands as a ledge or cliff with a bench on top (tile_height.gd _add_rock_beds, after erosion). Granite is hard but massive, so it makes rounded domes and knobs, not ledges.

spawn_pad_removed_note: Sonny 6 Nov 2026 (#473; Dave: 'we should not be adjust individual heights. it should be a systemic thing so it works across our entire world. the spawn point can just be moved'): the spawn pad (heights pinned level round the spawn) is gone; the spawn moved to x 53296 z 68080, naturally flat dry ground on a valley floor 2 m and more over any water (src/shared/spawn_point.gd).

valley_drain._note: Sonny 6 Nov 2026 (Dave: 'smoothing the surrounding area so it flows towards the river'): dry ground beside a river that lies lower than the water is raised to the water plus height_m, rising grade_per_m per metre away, within reach_m; a ridge stops it (tile_valley_drain.gd).
valley_drain.drain_hollows_note: Sonny 7 Nov 2026: after every pass that shapes the ground (banks, rolling, mend, mouths, drain) each dry closed hollow is raised to its spill, so rain cannot pool in a dip with no outlet on dry land; rivers, lakes, the sea and the frame edge are the outlets (tile_valley_drain.gd drain_hollows).

drainage.route_over_note: Sonny 6 Nov 2026 (Dave: rivers on the real valley floor): false routes the rivers over the finished ground (strata and scree included, both laid by world position so tiles still agree), not the raw pre-strata copy, so the river follows the lowest line the player sees.
drainage.river_extra_depth_note: Sonny 7 Nov 2026, later: back to 5 with max_depth_m 8 and bank_cut_slope 0 (Dino bisect: the 6 m carve doubled the dried pond cells and failed test_head_pond_fill; the bank cut changed nothing). The shallower valleys Dave wants come with natural rivers (P2), where depth follows flow. Earlier: Sonny 7 Nov 2026 (Dave: 'too deep ... 12 m at the valley floor ... maybe 6 with gentler slopes'): back to 0, with max_depth_m 6 and bank_cut_slope. Was 5 (6 Nov, Dave: 'cut them an extra 5 m deeper'): the centre bed and the water sink this much more, growing from the river threshold to full at 4 x it (drainage_channels.gd _stamp); the valleys follow the lower water.

banks._note: Sonny 3 Nov 2026 (no patchy riverbeds): a dry cell next to water higher than its ground is raised to that water plus height_m, by at most max_raise_m, so a channel across a hillside has a bank on its downhill side (tile_drainage.gd _build_banks). v2 (05:55): max_raise_m 1.5 -> 3 (759 of 919 still-leaking rim cells were at the cap); a bank taller than shoulder_drop_m raises the dry ground outside it to its top less shoulder_drop_m (at most half its lift), so it slopes away. v3 (Sonny 6 Nov 2026, Dave x 52935 z 69453: water spilling out of the beds into wetlands): height_m 0.2 -> 0.8 (the settled water stands up to ~0.9 m over the painted level on steep reaches) and every dry cell under the water plus height_m is a bank, not only those under the water.
banks.enabled_note: Back on (Sonny 7 Nov 2026, Dino bisect on tile 3,4: with them off, rule-carved rivers on side slopes leaked and test_river_surface and test_head_pond_fill failed; the dykes go for good with natural rivers, docs/water/terrain_water_pipeline.md P2). Was: Sonny 7 Nov 2026 (Dave x 54413 z 66833: 'there shouldnt be any bank dykes the river should have carved a valley nice and smooth'): off. The raised lips held ponds behind them. Ground lower than a river is now handled only by the valley drain (raised to slope up from the water, no lip) and drain_hollows.

drainage.dry_unsourced_note: Sonny 7 Nov 2026: off for now (Dino bisect on tile 3,4: drying sourceless heads left carved dry reaches whose junctions settled as falls, 46 extra cells over 4 m above their bank). Every head gets a source in natural rivers instead (P3).
drainage.lake_needs_river_out_note: Sonny 7 Nov 2026 (Dave x 53453 z 68888: ponds on the shelves above the river with no stream in or out): a natural hollow keeps a lake only when its catchment reaches river_start_km2, so a river runs out of it; every other hollow, shallow ones included, is filled in so it drains (tile_drainage.gd). valley_drain drain_hollows does the same for dry hollows the later passes leave.
drainage.bank_cut_note: Sonny 7 Nov 2026 (Dave: gentler slopes): beside each river the ground is cut to a bank rising this much per metre (about 17 degrees) from 0.2 m above the water at its edge until it meets the old ground (drainage_channels.gd _soften_banks); the water keeps its width. max_depth_m was 8.
drainage.mouth_grow_note: Dave 5 Nov 2026: rivers get deeper and a little wider toward the ocean. Over the last mouth_grow_m of a river that reaches the coast the channel widens to mouth_widen times and the centre bed sinks up to mouth_deepen_m more (drainage_channels.gd _toward_mouth); the estuary (estuary_*) takes over in the last few hundred metres.

natural.note: Natural rivers (GENERATOR_NOTES.md): the rivers are the drainage's own lines, bent on flat ground and carved from the flow; no ponds or craters. Width = width_base_m + width_per_sqrt_km2_m x sqrt(km2 drained), depth = depth_base_m + depth_per_km2_pow04_m x km2^0.4; the sideways swing is up to amp_widths x width (x noise_gain, capped) where the fall is under slope_flat, in knot_widths x width wavelengths, never up a bank more than valley_limit_m.

water.note: Hydrology on the 8 m height map. Rain falls evenly; each cell passes its water downhill. Rivers start where the catchment passes river_start_km2. Pits are filled unless they are big enough to be lakes.
water.head_note: A river head gets a spring pond and a narrowing first stretch; a steep drop gets a plunge pool at its foot (owner, 2026-10-17).
water.river_min_fall_note: Owner (2026-10-18): rivers only run downhill from source to sea; the bed falls at least this much per meter and cuts through rises.
water.head_pond_note: Owner (2026-10-19): the river climbs to the first flat enough ground and ends in a simple pond about 15 m deep (30-40 m across, then twice as wide on 2026-10-19 because ponds looked as wide as their streams: 70 m), with a spring in it that fills it until it overflows.
water.head_pond_size_note: Owner (2026-10-19): head ponds vary from head_pond_diameter_m up to head_pond_diameter_max_m (small lakes). Each draws a size, most stay small, and it only grows while the flat ground still holds it with its shore, so ponds near slopes stay small. The stream out of a bigger pond starts wider.
water.spring_size_note: Owner (2026-10-20): one spring per head pond; ponds up to this width get the base flow, bigger ponds get flow in step with their diameter (a 250 m pond pours twice as much), and the brook depth floor uses the same flow.
water.stream_depth_note: Owner (2026-10-20): the brook was too shallow and the water left it. Every brook and river is cut at least as deep as the flow it must carry (base spring flow times spring_rate_max: twice the x10 start flow since 2026-10-20, when every spring starts at x10; flood keys above that may overflow) plus a freeboard, and never under a minimum; brook beds only fall.
water.brook_lip_note: Owner (2026-10-20): a brook stays carved to its full depth all the way to the ledge edge, then pours over as a waterfall. A ledge is where the land drops this much within two samples (16 m); past it the brook bed holds its height and only cuts where land stands above it.
water.channel_notch_note: Owner report (2026-10-20, build 200): the water left the head ponds as a sheet 2 to 12 cm thick over the flat outlet and brook bed, too thin to draw, so no river seemed to leave the pond. Every brook and river bed is a shallow V: the middle is cut this much (at least, or this share of the width) below the bank toes, so normal flow gathers in the middle and shows. The outlet drop is 1.5 m at its edges and 1.5 m plus the notch in the middle.
water.straight_lip_note: Owner (2026-10-21, Dave): a lump of dirt blocked the river between pond B and its first fall (the brook's fall line hooked round a hill tip). The river leaves a pond for its first lip (ground this far under its outlet sill) by the straight way, cut through what stands between unless the lip is further than straight_lip_max_m or the line crosses ground more than straight_lip_rise_m above the pond. TileWater._straight_to_lip.
water.terrace_note: WIDTH (Dave 2026-10-21, TERRAIN_VERSION 25): a chute is as wide as the river that feeds it (the river width at its lip, whole cells, terrace_width_max_m only a safety cap), one constant width down the run. NEVER STEPS (Dave 2026-10-21): terrace_single_chute makes each steep run ONE clean chute (one face from the lip to the foot level, a plunge pool 0.4 x drop deep, capped 4 m, at its foot where the land is within chute_foot_land_m of the bed); a cliff onto a plateau is followed by a river reach and the next chute. Older text: Owner (2026-10-21, Dave): with the sim drawing the water, waterfalls must be flat and straight down until they hit the ground, and a cascade needs several. Where the bed falls faster than terrace_slope (m per m, over terrace_window_m) it becomes a staircase of flat treads and one-sample vertical faces: steps about terrace_drop_m high (taller on steeper ground, since a step is never shorter than terrace_step_min_m of run), the channel a multiple of 8 m wide between terrace_width_min_m and _max_m, banks terrace_bank (and terrace_face_bank beside the faces, near vertical). TileWater._terrace.
water.estuary_note: Owner (2026-10-20, Dave): rivers ran up to the ocean and stopped short, a step of a meter or more between the river water and the sea. A river that ends in the sea gets an estuary: over its last estuary_m (240 m) the bed sinks linearly to estuary_depth_m under sea level and the channel widens to estuary_widen times, so the sea comes up the channel and the water meets it at one level (TileWater, rivers loop).
water.river_from_pond_note: Owner (2026-10-20, Dave): place the ponds first, then the rivers, and start each river from the middle of its pond. A river with a world head pond is cut as one channel from the pond along its brook line to the head and on (TileWater._join_pond); inside the pond its line is a gentle ramp (spillway_slope) from the sill down into the bowl, so the spill is never a thin film over a steep drop. Water drawn from 12 cm (water_sim.gd WET_M).
water.head_pond_outlet_note: Owner (2026-10-20): ponds are made first and rivers cut last, but a river never reshapes a pond: across the shore no cut goes below the pond's sill (1.5 m under its lip) at the water's edge, falling by this much per meter outward, so the outlet runs smoothly down out of the pond.
water.head_pond_climb_note: A pond climbs at most this far above its river head looking for flat ground, so it does not end up on a summit far above the river (owner, 2026-10-19).
water.head_pond_setback_note: Owner (2026-10-19): the pond sits up to this far back from the edge of the flat ground it is on, so its stream runs across the flat to the edge before dropping.
water.head_pond_shore_note: Owner (2026-10-19): the pond sits on a flat bench this wide around its water (2026-10-19: 40 m, so the stream runs across the flat; the ground there may vary at most twice head_pond_max_rim_range_m before the bench levels it), the land sloping gently away (blended over head_pond_wall_fade_m, longer where the land is far off), never like a crater.
water.head_pond_search_note: With no flat ground just above a river head, the pond moves up to the first flat ground within this distance uphill and a straight brook runs down to the head (owner, 2026-10-19).
water.head_straighten_note: A source river's first stretch on ground steeper than head_straighten_slope runs straight down the fall line instead of following the coarse world path (owner, 2026-10-19). Not within head_straighten_edge_samples of the frame edge, where the neighbor tile carves the same river.
water.network_meander_note: Sideways push of the world river curves so they do not follow the 160 m grid. Each octave is a smooth random field; amplitude is the typical push in meters. Keep the total well under one 160 m cell.
water.bank_reach_note: Where a river bed is cut well below the ground its banks slope back up to this far, so deep cuts become valleys instead of cliffs (owner, 2026-10-19).

starter_river.note: A river from the biggest highland lake to the head of the starter bay, following the easiest valley route. Extra water is fed in at the source so it is a real river. Owner (2026-10-19): turned off; its route climbed a hill and cut a canyon through it, and rivers now come only from head ponds along real valleys. The spawn then sits at the bay head.

climate.note: Climate, moisture, biome, soil and fertility for one tile. Temperature comes from latitude and height. Moisture comes from a wet-air sweep along the prevailing wind (wet over sea, drier over land, much drier behind mountains) plus nearness to fresh water. Thresholds are in degrees C, 0 to 1 moisture, degrees of slope and meters.

soil.clay_edge_note: Bare clay shows at the surface only this close to fresh water (owner, 2026-10-17); elsewhere clay lies under topsoil.

summit_pluton.note: Hard rock under the tall peaks (docs/water/watershed_rebuild_design.md, A1 rule 3, 8 Nov 2026): every world-map summit at or above min_summit_m stands on a granite intrusion centred on it. Its roof is roof_above_summit_share above the summit at the centre (so above the summit tent too) and falls to edge_share of the summit height at the ellipse edge, so the upper massif is granite. Not in volcanic cells. Not one disc (8 Nov 2026, after run c793c47c wore a round dome in a circular cliff ring): a core of core_radius_share x the radius under the summit, then up to lobes.max lobes, one along each of the summit's spurs (sketch_rules standing.tip_spurs), each an ellipse of radius_share x the radius stretched along the spur (aspect) and centred offset_share x the radius out, so the granite runs under the ridges and its edge is lobed, as real batholiths are clusters of plutons.

karst.count_note: Off (Dave: caves only at river starts; coordinator 7 Nov 2026). Goblins, bears and cave life use the spring caves.

sea_cave.count_note: Off (Dave: caves only at river starts; coordinator 7 Nov 2026). Goblins, bears and cave life use the spring caves.

spring_cave._note: Dave 3 Nov 2026: a brook head on a hillside comes out of a cave about 100 m deep rising gently, the spring at the back, side branches with dens; some get 2 or 3 spring passages (extra_passage_chance: 2 or more, 3); each spring gives spring_m3_s_per_km2 x the head catchment km2 and their flows add up; no cave where the main passage finds under min_length_m of room.
spring_cave.hill_note: Sonny 6 Nov 2026 (Dave: a river starting at the base or on the side of a hill or mountain gets a cave, on flat ground a head pond): a brook head flatter than min_slope_deg still gets a cave when the ground rises hill_rise_m within hill_reach_m (the foot of a hill).
spring_cave.min_sea_note: Sonny 6 Nov 2026 (Dave: caves "only show up way inland wherever the river starts"): no spring cave at a brook head with the sea within this many metres (tile_sites.gd inland_mask, on the whole frame so tiles agree). The terrain 59 bake had 30 of its 96 caves within 1 km of the sea.
spring_cave._head_max_start_note: Dave 6 Nov 2026 (x 52441 z 68924, a cave not at a river start): a cave mouth only where no river within 16 m drains more than 1.6 times river_start_km2, so caves open at the heads of brooks, never beside a river already running.
spring_cave._sizes_note: Dave 4 Nov 2026: some caves small, some medium, some large (a size the hill has no room for falls back to the next smaller one); the top-level values are the medium cave. The mouth is as wide as the river at the head and narrows to the passage over taper_min_m or a third of the passage; den tunnels climb den_rise and end in a den hollow; bones at entrances and far ends; stalagmites and stalactites in large caves' big chambers and wide passages.
spring_cave.spring_per_mouth_note: Dave 5 Nov 2026: a wide river needs many spring pools; one spring passage per 6 m of the river's width at the mouth, up to the size's max_springs (small 1, medium 3, large 6), their flows joining on the way out.

runtime_terrain.note: Runtime voxel generator (plan step 14). Not baked: the voxels are worked out from the tile maps when a block is needed. detail: small height noise added on land (faded out on water); octaves finer than two voxels are skipped at coarse LODs. sdf_band_voxels: voxels written one by one on each side of the surface; the rest of the column is filled in runs. placeholder_depth_m: sea floor of a tile with no file. Caves are carved up to cave_max_lod, ore is written up to ore_max_lod.

runtime_flora.note: Runtime flora (plan step 15). Not baked: placed per chunk from biome, moisture, ground shape and the tile's flora seed, with species from data/tables/flora.json. chunk_m: chunk size (must divide the tile size). density: multiplies every species' per-hectare figure; it changes item ids, so freeze it once players remove trees. patchiness (0 to 1) and patch_m: a smooth noise field of that wavelength thins trees into glades (shrubs no longer follow it: they also grow under the trees). view_m: how far each kind is drawn (owner 2026-10-18: trees cut from 560 to 420 m and shrubs from 300 to 160 m to pay for denser woods and three times the shrubs; the extra plants sit in the far ring, unnoticed from the ground; 2026-10-19: trees cut again to 300 m and shrubs to 120 m because the world loaded slower, which takes the flora chunks around the player from about 16 to 10; 2026-10-19 again: trees and shrubs 25% shorter, to 225 m and 90 m, for loading speed). Owner 2026-10-19 (later): only the big things far: trees out to 450 m, shrubs 45 m and small plants 60 m; chunks beyond the shrub and plant range come with their trees only (flora_view.gd full_m). near_m: full-detail models out to this distance, cheap far models beyond (tree 150 m). collision_m: trees and shrubs this close to the player get collision.
